stem: The student wants to provide an example of a mutually beneficial relationship between two species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mutualism is a relationship between two species in which both species benefit.
• Mutualistic relationships are common among species that live on coral reefs.
• The bluestreak cleaner wrasse is a small reef fish that removes parasites from the bodies of larger reef fish.
• The wrasse gets a meal of parasites, and the larger fish is rid of pests that could harm it.
• Many reef fish visit the wrasse's "cleaning stations" several times a day.
choices: Mutualism, in which two species both benefit, is a type of relationship common among the species living on coral reefs.
The bluestreak cleaner wrasse and the larger reef fish it cleans benefit each other: the wrasse gets a meal, and the larger fish loses its parasites.
Larger reef fish benefit from the bluestreak cleaner wrasse, which gains nothing for itself by removing their parasites.
The bluestreak cleaner wrasse, a small reef fish, removes parasites from the larger fish that visit its cleaning stations.
explanation: The goal asks for an example, so you need one named pair of species, and you need to show that the relationship is mutually beneficial. The notes call this 'mutualism'. Choice B names the bluestreak cleaner wrasse and the larger fish it cleans, and it states what each one gains. That makes it a specific instance of the property the goal names.

A.why: You chose the category-level definition. This choice describes mutualism in general and names no particular species, so it makes a generalization instead of giving an example.

C.why: You may have chosen this because it names a specific species. However, it says the wrasse gains nothing, and the notes say the wrasse gets a meal. A relationship that benefits only one side is not mutually beneficial.

D.why: This choice names a specific instance, but it shows only one side of the benefit: the larger fish lose their parasites. It never says what the wrasse gains, so it doesn't show that the relationship is mutually beneficial.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about slow slip events. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Slow slip events are fault movements that unfold over days to months rather than over seconds.
• They release built-up stress gradually and generally produce no shaking that people can feel.
• Along the Cascadia subduction zone in the Pacific Northwest, slow slip events have recurred roughly every 14 months.
• Along New Zealand's Hikurangi margin, shallow slow slip events recur about every 18 to 24 months.
• Researchers are studying whether slow slip events might raise the short-term likelihood of larger earthquakes.
choices: Along the Cascadia subduction zone in the Pacific Northwest, slow slip events have recurred roughly every 14 months.
Slow slip events recur about every 14 months in Cascadia, whereas they recur every 18 to 24 months along the Hikurangi margin.
Slow slip events unfold over days to months, releasing stress gradually and generally without shaking that people can feel.
Slow slip events are reliably followed by larger earthquakes, so seismologists treat them as warnings of coming shaking.
explanation: A generalization makes a claim about the whole category, and no single location or event is its subject. Choice C makes 'slow slip events' as a group its subject and states what is true of them in general: how long they last and how they release stress.

A.why: You picked the wrong level. This choice describes slow slip events in one specific place, Cascadia, so it gives an example instead of a generalization about the category.

B.why: This is the wrong level again. Comparing two specific locations is not a generalization. The relation word 'whereas' makes it a strong comparison, but the goal didn't ask for one.

D.why: The notes say only that researchers are studying whether slow slip events *might* raise the likelihood of larger earthquakes. Saying they are 'reliably followed' by earthquakes claims far more than the notes support.

stem: The student wants to present a specific example of resist dyeing and explain how it works. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Resist dyeing is any method of patterning cloth by preventing dye from reaching certain areas of the fabric.
• Batik is a technique that has been practiced on the Indonesian island of Java for centuries.
• In batik, artisans apply hot wax to parts of a fabric before dyeing it.
• The waxed areas keep their original color when the cloth is dyed.
• In 2009, UNESCO recognized Indonesian batik as part of the world's Intangible Cultural Heritage.
choices: Batik is a resist-dyeing technique: artisans apply hot wax to fabric, and the waxed areas keep their original color when the cloth is dyed.
In resist dyeing, cloth is given a pattern by a method that prevents dye from reaching certain areas of the fabric.
Batik, a technique practiced on Java for centuries, was recognized by UNESCO in 2009 as Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Batik is a resist-dyeing technique in which artisans apply hot wax to fabric after it has been dyed to seal in the color.
explanation: The goal has two parts: name a specific example, and explain how it works as resist dyeing. Choice A names batik, labels it a resist-dyeing technique, and describes how it works: wax keeps dye from reaching certain areas, so those areas stay their original color.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. You chose the general definition of the category, but it names no specific technique, so it gives no example.

C.why: This choice names a specific instance, but it gives historical details instead of how the technique works. It never connects batik to resist dyeing.

D.why: The notes say the wax goes on *before* dyeing, so that dye can't reach those areas. Putting the wax on after dyeing reverses the process and removes the 'resist'.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about how memory B cells respond to a pathogen they have encountered before. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Memory B cells are long-lived immune cells that form after an infection or a vaccination.
• When the body is exposed again to the same pathogen, memory B cells produce antibodies against it.
• This second response is faster and produces more antibodies than the body's response to the first exposure.
• One study detected memory B cells specific to the smallpox vaccine in some people vaccinated more than 50 years earlier.
• Memory B cells do not protect against pathogens the body has never encountered.
choices: Memory B cells specific to the smallpox vaccine were detected in some people vaccinated more than 50 years earlier.
Memory B cells are long-lived immune cells that form in the body after an infection or after a vaccination.
Memory B cells give people lifelong protection against every pathogen their immune systems have ever encountered.
When memory B cells meet a pathogen again, they produce antibodies faster and in greater amounts than in the first response.
explanation: The goal asks for two things: a claim about memory B cells as a category, and a claim about one topic, how they respond to a pathogen they've met before. Only the third note covers that response. Choice D turns that note into a general statement about all memory B cells, with no single case as its subject.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You chose one specific study about one vaccine, which is an example, not a generalization about the category.

B.why: This choice is at the right level because it's general, but it addresses the wrong topic. It says how memory B cells form, not how they respond to a pathogen they've encountered before.

C.why: Nothing in the notes supports 'lifelong' protection against 'every' pathogen. One study found cells lasting 50 years against one vaccine, and that doesn't justify such a sweeping claim.

stem: The student wants to provide an example of a printmaking method in which ink is held below the surface of the printing plate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In intaglio printmaking, ink is held in grooves cut below the surface of a metal plate.
• Paper pressed onto the plate under great pressure pulls the ink out of the grooves.
• Drypoint is one form of intaglio.
• In drypoint, an artist scratches lines directly into a copper plate with a sharp steel needle.
• In relief methods such as woodcut, by contrast, ink sits on raised surfaces left after the background is carved away.
choices: In intaglio printmaking, ink is held in grooves that have been cut below the surface of a metal printing plate.
Drypoint, in which an artist scratches lines into a copper plate with a needle, is an intaglio method, so its ink sits in grooves.
In drypoint, an artist uses a sharp steel needle to scratch lines directly into the surface of a copper plate.
Woodcut is a printmaking method in which ink is held in grooves carved below the surface of a wooden block.
explanation: The goal uses the phrase 'held below the surface', but the notes never say drypoint works that way. They say intaglio does, and that drypoint is a form of intaglio. Choice B names a specific method, drypoint, and connects it to intaglio, which ties it to the property the goal asks about: ink held in grooves below the plate's surface.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You chose the statement about the category, intaglio in general, which names no specific method. The goal asked for an example.

C.why: This choice names drypoint, but it only describes scratching lines. It never says drypoint is intaglio or that the ink sits below the surface. The property is stated in a different note, so this choice misses it.

D.why: The notes say that in woodcut, ink sits on *raised* surfaces. That's the opposite of the property the goal names, so woodcut can't be the example.
